verses.text: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the inland regions and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples.
He asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They answered, “We haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
He asked, “Then what baptism did you receive?” They replied, “John’s baptism.”
Paul said, “John baptized people as a sign of turning back to God. He told them to believe in the one coming after him—that is, Jesus.”
When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
When Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them. They spoke in other languages and prophesied.
There were about twelve men in all.
Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly for three months, discussing and persuading them about God’s Kingdom.

But some became stubborn and refused to believe. They spoke against the Way in front of everyone, so Paul left them. He took the disciples with him and held daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
This went on for two years, so that everyone living in Asia, both Jews and Greeks, heard the Lord’s message.
God performed extraordinary miracles through Paul.
People took cloths and aprons that had touched him to the sick, and their diseases left them and evil spirits came out.
Some traveling Jewish exorcists tried to use the Lord Jesus’ name over people with evil spirits. They said, “I command you by the Jesus Paul preaches.”
Seven sons of a Jewish chief priest named Sceva were doing this.
But the evil spirit answered, “I know Jesus, and I know Paul. Who are you?”
Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them. They fled from the house naked and wounded.
Everyone in Ephesus, Jews and Greeks alike, heard about this. Fear came over them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was honored.
Many who had become believers came forward, admitting and describing what they had done.
A number of people who practiced magic brought their books together and burned them in front of everyone. They calculated the value: fifty thousand pieces of silver.
In this way the Lord’s word spread powerfully and kept growing.
After these events, Paul decided in the Spirit to travel through Macedonia and Achaia and then go to Jerusalem. He said, “After I’ve been there, I must also see Rome.”
He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, ahead to Macedonia, while he stayed in Asia for a while.
Around that time, a serious disturbance broke out over the Way.
A silversmith named Demetrius made silver shrines of Artemis, bringing in good business for the craftsmen.
He gathered them and other workers in the same trade and said, “Men, you know this work is how we make our living.
“You can see and hear that Paul has persuaded many people, not only here in Ephesus but throughout almost all Asia. He says that handmade gods aren’t really gods.
“There’s a risk our trade will lose its good name. And the temple of the great goddess Artemis could be discredited, with her magnificence brought down—she whom all Asia and the world worship.”
When they heard this, they became furious and shouted, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
Confusion spread through the whole city. The crowd rushed together into the theater, dragging along Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s travel companions from Macedonia.
Paul wanted to go in and address the crowd, but the disciples wouldn’t let him.
Even some Asiarchs who were his friends sent word, urging him not to risk going into the theater.
Some people in the crowd shouted one thing and others another. The meeting was a total mess, and most didn’t even know why they were there.
The Jews pushed Alexander forward from the crowd. He motioned for silence and tried to defend himself to the people.
But when the crowd realized he was a Jew, they all shouted together for about two hours, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
At last the city clerk quieted the crowd and said, “People of Ephesus, everyone knows that Ephesus is guardian of the temple of great Artemis and of her image that fell from Zeus.
“Since no one can deny this, you should calm down and not do anything rash.
“You brought these men here, but they haven’t robbed temples or insulted our goddess.
“If Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a case against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls. Let them bring their charges there.
“If you have any other issue, it must be settled in a lawful assembly.
“We’re in danger of being charged with rioting over what happened today. We have no good reason for this gathering, and we won’t be able to explain this disorder.”
After saying this, he dismissed the assembly.
